scenes.heading: What quantitative reasoning tests
scenes.sub: Find the rule, test it, use it
scenes.say: Quantitative reasoning questions hide a rule inside numbers, shapes or tables. Your job is to find it, check it and use it. Let us see what the section looks like and how to beat the clock.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A detective checks every alibi before arresting a suspect
scenes.science: Your first rule is a suspect: test it on every term or row
scenes.breaks: a detective may have days. You have about fifty seconds, so test quickly and move on.
scenes.say: Think like a detective. A good detective never arrests the first suspect without checking the alibi. Your first idea for a rule is a suspect too. Test it on every number or row before you trust it. The difference is time: a detective has days, you have under a minute.

scenes.heading: Six question types
scenes.say: You will meet six main types: number sequences, number grids, symbol puzzles, comparing quantities, shape patterns, and quick tables and graphs. Each one has its own lesson in this chapter.

scenes.heading: Spot, test, choose
steps: Find a rule in the first part
Work out the answer, then find it
scenes.say: Use the same routine every time. Spot the type. Find a rule from the first pair or row. Test it on every part. Then work out your answer before you read the options, because the options are built from common mistakes.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: What comes next? 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, ?
scenes.say: Three, seven, eleven, fifteen, nineteen. It is a sequence. The first gap is four. Test it: every gap is four. So the next number is nineteen plus four, which is twenty-three.
scenes.caption: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19: every gap is 4, so the next number is 19 + 4 = 23.

scenes.heading: Your pace
scenes.say: Now timing. Thirty minutes is one thousand eight hundred seconds. Shared between thirty-five questions, that is about fifty-one seconds each.
scenes.caption: 30 minutes = 1800 seconds. 1800 ÷ 35 ≈ 51 seconds per question.

scenes.heading: Stuck on a question?
scenes.say: If you are stuck after about ninety seconds, cross out what is impossible, guess, mark it and move on. Come back on a second pass. Do not fight one question for minutes, and never leave a blank.

points: QR tests finding and using rules
scenes.say: Quick recap. Quantitative reasoning tests finding and using rules. Learn the six types. Spot, test, choose. Keep to about fifty-one seconds a question, and guess, mark and move rather than leave a blank. Now try the practice questions!
